cases.title: No. 129 Squadron at the Varengeville battery
cases.mission: Twelve Spitfires of No. 129 Squadron supported No. 4 Commando's final assault on the six-gun coastal battery west of Dieppe. The Canadian Army history places the fighters' attack at 06:20.
cases.effect: The commandos reached the gun positions and destroyed all six guns before withdrawing. The RAF narrative identifies the squadron. The army history places its attack alongside the final advance and records an earlier ammunition explosion at about 06:07.
cases.limit: The commandos credited their mortar for the earlier explosion. German accounts credited an aircraft. Stacey favoured the mortar because the Air Force Commander's report records no strike at 06:07.

cases.title: Cover for the ships during the withdrawal
cases.mission: No. 403 Squadron RCAF left at 11:15 and brought all twelve aircraft back at 13:15. Its 16:20 patrol saw the homeward convoy. On No. 411 Squadron's last patrol, its pilots attacked a Do 217 near the returning ships.
cases.effect: The No. 411 account places the bomber's release about a mile from the convoy. Captain Hughes-Hallett, commanding the naval force, credited No. 11 Group for covering his ships and considered the loss of one ship to bombing unusually fortunate. The Admiralty diary names HMS Berkeley as disabled by bombing and subsequently sunk.
cases.limit: The naval commander assessed the whole force. Neither the ship record nor the squadron entries identify the ship protected by the 411 encounter or quantify how many hits the patrols prevented.

cases.title: Smoke over the approaches at first light
cases.mission: Nos. 13 and 614 Squadrons supplied Blenheims for smoke and No. 226 supplied Bostons. The RAF records a screen off the eastern headland in the 04:45–05:50 period.
cases.effect: The German commander in the west reported that smoke obscured the landing craft from defenders ashore. His report attributed the screen to ships or aircraft. Later, the RAF narrative records a request for fresh smoke at the east headland when no aircraft was immediately ready.
cases.limit: The reports locate the obstruction from shore and the gap in renewed cover. Neither separates the smoke from each ship or squadron.

cases.title: What the attack on Abbeville changed
cases.mission: The 97th Bombardment Group attacked the German fighter field at Abbeville–Drucat. The RAF account names Nos. 64, 401 and 611 as Spitfire escorts. The RCAF history describes four escort squadrons and includes No. 402.
cases.effect: The RAF narrative reports that the airfield was unusable for approximately two hours, citing a Luftflotte 3 appreciation. The Canadian air history judges that the two diversions failed to draw pressure away from the evacuation.
cases.limit: A temporary closure at one field and fighter opposition over the beaches measure different effects. The sources disagree on the escort roster, and neither quantifies interceptions prevented.

cases.title: Typhoon escorts on the Ostend diversion
cases.mission: At 11:15, Nos. 56, 266 and 609 Squadrons escorted nine Defiants in a diversion towards Ostend while the Dieppe force withdrew.
cases.effect: Fighter Command recorded no German reaction to this feint. Allied fighter cover over Dieppe had already increased for the evacuation.
cases.limit: The escort report records what the crews observed. It does not show whether a German controller redirected aircraft out of their sight.

cases.title: German attacks on the shipping
cases.mission: The fighter-bomber Staffeln of JG 2 and JG 26 attacked shipping off Dieppe. German claim records also place bomber crews of 4. and 5./KG 40 in combat. British wireless intelligence distinguished at least 69 Do 217s and 17 Ju 88s across the long-range bomber response.
cases.effect: The Admiralty's diary records that bombing disabled HMS Berkeley and that she had to be sunk. Chris Goss attributes the hit to two aircraft of 10.(Jabo)/JG 2. Aircrew of 5./KG 40 claimed Spitfires off Dieppe late in the afternoon.
cases.limit: The naval diary confirms the damage without naming the attackers. The KG 40 claims establish presence. A matched Allied loss return is needed to verify any corresponding aircraft loss.

cases.title: What the Mustang crews could report inland
cases.mission: Four army co-operation squadrons searched the roads for reinforcements. On No. 414 Squadron's first flight, Frederick Clarke and Hollis Hills were sent to check the Abbeville–Dieppe road. Hills recalled losing sight of his leader in darkness. Both returned to Gatwick.
cases.effect: Hills could see no traffic on the first flight. The RCAF history reports that the four squadrons' only positive sighting was of three to five supposed light tanks south of Dieppe. It concludes the identification was mistaken and that the Germans dealt with the landing from local resources.
cases.limit: The four-squadron reconnaissance effort cost ten aircraft missing. The evidence does not attribute the tank report to No. 414 or establish that a commander changed a decision on receiving it.

Allied.effort: 74 allocated squadrons in nine roles. RAF history counts 2,614 RAF and USAAF sorties over the operation, including seven Coastal Command sorties.
Allied.losses: The RAF narrative reports 106 aircraft lost in its own force categories. Three No. 403 aircraft failed to return from its first patrol. All twelve returned from its second.
Allied.effect: The naval commander credited the cover. No. 411 observed a bomber release about a mile from the convoy, while HMS Berkeley was disabled by bombing and scuttled.

Axis.effort: Six identified fighter Gruppen and two dedicated fighter-bomber Staffeln. British wireless intelligence counted at least 86 long-range bombers. A complete German strike and reconnaissance order remains open.
Axis.losses: German records summarized by the RAF list 25 bombers and 23 fighters destroyed, plus 16 bombers and eight fighters damaged. Crew combat claims have a separate basis.
Axis.effect: German ground observers reported that smoke obscured landing craft. German attacks reached the shipping. The naval diary confirms the loss of Berkeley without identifying the attacking unit.
